reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that 0.1 at.% boron induces intergranular borides and improves grain boundary cohesion and ductility in a specific refractory HEA (HfMoNbTaTiZr). However, it does not provide evidence for Ti-Ni-primary HEAs, nor does it demonstrate improved elevated-temperature mechanical properties like microhardness or grain-size stability under prolonged heating, which are key premises of the hypothesis.
premises: Boron addition induces intergranular boride precipitates in HEAs
Intergranular borides enhance grain boundary cohesion
Enhanced grain boundary cohesion improves elevated-temperature mechanical properties
0.1 at.% boron is sufficient to achieve these effects
These effects observed in refractory HEAs will transfer to Ti-Ni-primary HEAs
